performance_interpretation: TERMINAL OUTCOME IS A COLLECTION FAILURE, NOT A MEASURED BOTTLENECK. Five msprof attempts (two metrics rounds covering four workloads, plus one instruction round and one isolated metrics retry on selu_-timing-11) all returned status=failed with error 'msprof base collection exited successfully without profile completion marker', per-profile capabilities empty, zero artifacts, and only the six manifest.json files on disk. Nothing was ever executed and parsed from the device counters, so this analysis contains NO profiler facts and NO artifact-backed findings; every statement below is derived only from the authoritative eval comparison in get_profile_context. PROCEDURAL CAVEAT worth checking first on the next attempt: round 2's candidate deliberately routes the hot path through a raw pybind launcher (compiled.run.launch) rather than Triton's NPULauncher dispatch, and _make_contig_launch() aborts to the ordinary launch only when enable_msprof_register_tensor is set. If the harness enables that flag the fallback should trigger, but if msprof instead instruments at a layer this raw call bypasses, msprof would complete with no operator records, which is exactly the symptom observed. This is a hypothesis about the failure, not a measurement, and it is untested. FROZEN-HYPOTHESIS VERDICT: the profiler evidence neither supports nor contradicts the round-2 hypothesis (host-dispatch removal helps only the nine launch-bound workloads); the profiler evidence is simply absent. The EVAL evidence supports it decisively. Before/after per workload: the nine small/medium cases fell from 15.97-17.51 us to 8.96-10.38 us (-37% to -49%, speedups 0.73-0.84 -> 1.03-1.23), while the three 4096x4096 cases moved by at most 0.39% (timing-3 -0.39%, timing-7 -0.02%, timing-11 -0.03%). That is the predicted signature: a pure host-side win capped by the residual call path, leaving device-bound work untouched. geo_mean 0.73012 -> 1.00156 (+37.18%). REGIME SPLIT FROM EVAL TIMING ALONE. (a) Launch-bound regime, nine workloads: latency is flat in numel, e.g. fp16 1024 elements 8.963 us versus fp16 1048576 elements 9.081 us - 1024x more data for +1.3% time - so the ~9-10 us floor is still call overhead, not device work; the remaining headroom here is host-side only and small in geo_mean terms. (b) Device-bound regime, three workloads: 81.61 us (fp16), 83.23 us (bf16), 82.66 us (fp32) at identical element count of 16777216. Converting to element rate gives 205.6, 201.6 and 203.0 Gelem/s - constant within 2.4% while the bytes moved differ by exactly 2x (67.1 MB vs 134.2 MB round trip). A memory-bandwidth-limited kernel cannot hold element rate constant while doubling bytes, and the declared target L2 is 176160768 bytes (168 MB), which exceeds the 134.2 MB fp32 working set, so HBM saturation is not the explanation either. The element rate is constant, therefore the limit scales with ELEMENTS, not bytes. The strongest candidate mechanism is per-element Vector-pipeline work: _selu_nomask() upcasts to fp32 three times in one expression (x.to(tl.float32) in the predicate, then twice inside tl.where, at lines 56/66/122) and evaluates tl.exp unconditionally on the whole 8192-lane fp32 tile, so fp16/bf16 inputs still pay full-width fp32 vector ops. CONSISTENCY WITH THE REFERENCE. The reference achieves 295.5 (fp16), 283.8 (bf16) and 339.9 (fp32) Gelem/s, i.e. 1.44x, 1.41x and 1.67x our element rate, and - informatively - the reference's fp32 case (49.36 us) is FASTER than its fp16 (56.77 us) and bf16 (59.11 us) cases despite moving twice the bytes. A vendor kernel whose cost tracks element count and whose fp32 case is cheapest is consistent with native-dtype vector math, again arguing against a bandwidth limit in either implementation. CAUTION: the same element-count constancy is also predicted by a per-program/per-tile fixed-overhead limit, because all three large cases use the identical grid of 2048 programs (n=16777216, _pick_block returns _BLOCK_MAX=8192). The eval data cannot separate 'per-element fp32 vector work' from 'per-program overhead' - only a device counter capture or a deliberate tile-count change can. That ambiguity is the main open question and the next experiment is built to resolve it.

next_experiment.action_description: Add a constexpr-selected native-dtype math branch to the nomask kernel and use it only for the large contiguous tile. In _selu_nomask, when a new constexpr flag (e.g. NATIVE_MATH) is set, hoist a single conversion-free path that computes the selu predicate, tl.exp and the 1.6732632423543772 multiply in the input dtype for fp16/bf16 inputs, casting only once at the store. Leave the existing fp32-tile expression byte-identical for fp32 inputs and for every non-large specialization. Gate the new branch so it is compiled only when the chosen tile is the large tile (BLOCK >= 8192, i.e. the numel >= 65536 fast path), so the nine launch-bound specializations, their cache keys and their bound raw launches are unchanged. Also hoist the repeated x.to(tl.float32) in the retained fp32 expression into one local (lines 56, 66, 122) as a zero-risk companion change, since three textual casts of the same value widen vector pressure if the compiler does not CSE them.
next_experiment.expected_impact: If the per-element fp32 Vector work hypothesis holds, selu_-timing-3 and selu_-timing-7 should move from 81.6/83.2 us toward the reference's 56.8/59.1 us (element rate 205 -> ~290 Gelem/s), lifting those two speedups from 0.70/0.71 to near 1.0 and raising geo_mean by roughly +0.04 to +0.05 on top of 1.00156. selu_-timing-11 (fp32) and all nine launch-bound cases must stay within noise. If the per-program-overhead alternative is the real limit instead, these two workloads will barely move, which is itself the decisive result: it would redirect the next round to the tile/grid axis (halving or doubling _BLOCK_MAX only for the large path) rather than to arithmetic.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: fp16/bf16 exp and the alpha multiply lose accuracy, roughly 1e-3 relative; the fp16/bf16 timing and correctness tolerances are rtol=atol=1.5e-2 with required_matched_ratio 1.0, leaving a wide budget, but all 24 correctness workloads must still pass and the fp32 tolerance is only 1e-4, which is why the fp32 path must not be touched. Changing the kernel body changes UB footprint and may change or fail compilation at BLOCK=8192 (the current tile was chosen as the largest that fits 192KB once the fp32 compute tile is materialized, so a native-dtype variant should shrink rather than grow it, but this is unverified). Rollback is confined to the new constexpr branch plus the hoisted local: restore the round-2 expression and drop the NATIVE_MATH flag, and the round-2 kernel and cache keys are recovered exactly. Do not bundle any tile-size or grid change into this round, or the two hypotheses will be confounded again.
success_criteria: Full correctness contract passes: all 24 selu_ correctness workloads PASSED with matched_ratio 1.0 for float16, bfloat16 and float32, including the empty, single-element, 1025-element, [7,9] and strided variants.
Headline geo_mean increases above the round-2 value of 1.001556545566768, driven by selu_-timing-3 and selu_-timing-7.

selu_-timing-3 and selu_-timing-7 latency moves materially toward the 56.8/59.1 us reference, i.e. element rate rises above roughly 250 Gelem/s; a move to within 10% of reference is the strong outcome.

No regression in the nine launch-bound workloads: selu_-timing-0/1/2/4/5/6/8/9/10 stay in the 8.9-10.5 us band (speedup >= 1.0) and selu_-timing-11 stays within noise of 82.66 us, confirming the change was correctly scoped to the large fp16/bf16 path.

If both large fp16/bf16 cases stay within noise, record the negative result and treat the per-element-vector hypothesis as falsified before attempting any further arithmetic change; the next round must then test program count (tile size for the large path only) instead.

open_questions: Why did msprof exit successfully without a profile completion marker on all four workloads, including the small control selu_-timing-6? Is the raw pybind launcher (compiled.run.launch) bypassing the msprof instrumentation layer that the ordinary Triton NPULauncher path provides, and did the enable_msprof_register_tensor fallback in _make_contig_launch actually fire?

Do the device counters confirm a Vector-pipeline limit for the three 4096x4096 cases, or do they show an MTE2/MTE3 limit that the constant element rate merely obscures? pipeline_utilization was advertised but never delivered.

Does large-input latency scale with program count or with element count? This needs either counters or a deliberate one-knob tile change on the large path; both large-regime hypotheses predict the current dtype-flat timing equally well.
Is the 168 MB L2 confirmed to serve the 134.2 MB fp32 working set across the 100 measured iterations? If it does, bandwidth arguments are further weakened, but no cache counter was captured.
